doc.title: Bruce Johnstone interviewed by Monk Rowe, Dunkirk, New York, October 11, 2013

title: Studio work, Chequers, and the move to Europe
summary: He became a busy studio and TV player and assistant musical director at Chequers, then sold instruments and sailed to Europe with his wife.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Busy, yeah. And from there it kind of transformed into studio work. And the last years I was in Australia I was assistant musical director of a big nightclub called Chequers, which used to have name American acts come through. And I was staff on four T.V. shows. So that was a regular four days a week I was doing that, plus I was doing recording sessions for back-up rock things. It was pretty much a seven day a week, 18- hour day existence. And it was great. The money was terrific. But in making it with that much intensity meant that you were just completely wiped out all the time. You didn’t have time to really develop anything new. So one night I went home and I said to my wife, “can we go to Europe?” And she said, “yeah, let’s go to Europe.” So we woke up the next morning and she said “did you say we’re going to Europe?” And I said, “yeah, let’s go.” So we looked at the shipping schedule and there was a ship leaving a week from then. So we got our passports, went down, sold a bunch of instruments, and got on the ship and went to Europe.
What would you have sold? Stuff that you said I don’t need this?
